context: Normalize each record's raw funding text and YC batch text. The funding parser reads at most one amount and one currency per text: the currency may be $, €, £, ¥, or the codes USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, RMB (also US$), before or after the number; numbers may use commas; multipliers k/thousand = 1,000, m/mn/million = 1,000,000, b/bn/billion = 1,000,000,000, 万 = 10,000, 亿 = 100,000,000; the amount is the exact decimal in that currency after the multiplier. It also reads at most one round: pre-seed, seed, or Series A-D, mapped to pre-seed, seed, series-a through series-d; no round is unknown. The text may not contain extra words, two amounts, or two currencies. The texts 'Undisclosed', 'not disclosed', 'n/a', 'unknown', or an empty string disclose no amount; such a text may still name a round. Convert every disclosed amount to whole US dollars with the fixed rate table USD 1, EUR 1.08, GBP 1.27, CNY 0.14, multiplying the amount by the rate and rounding halves away from zero (e.g. 13.5 becomes 14). The batch parser maps W, X, S, F and the full season names winter, spring, summer, fall to Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall; a two-digit year means 2000+yy, and years outside 2005-2030 are invalid. Keep records in input order with company names exactly as given; disclosed records get an integer funding_usd and undisclosed records get null; total_usd is the sum of all disclosed funding_usd (0 when none) and undisclosed counts the records with no disclosed amount.
